label: Fresh Spice
reason: Ginger and cardamom give distinct familiar routes within freshness.

choices.label: Gingery
choices.reference_note: Fresh Madagascar ginger oil illustrates the zesty ginger facet; its woody undertone need not fit every scent.

choices.label: Cardamom-like
choices.reference_note: Guatemalan cardamom seed oil illustrates fresh green spice, with herbal and camphor-like facets.

label: Hot Spice
reason: Baking cinnamon and clove differ enough to be useful choices.

choices.label: Cinnamony
choices.reference_note: Robertet cinnamon bark oil illustrates cinnamon spice with woody and powdery facets. It is not a pastry accord.

choices.label: Clove-like
choices.reference_note: IFF clove bud oil illustrates warm clove spice; the clove-studded orange comparison does not imply a citrus blend.

label: Savoury Spice
reason: Keep one clear cumin direction; do not invent an unsupported saffron equivalence.

choices.label: Cumin-like
choices.reference_note: Biolandes Cumin Seeds Oil E7187 illustrates the cumin facet of a spice mix. The source identifies Cuminum cyminum, not black cumin (Nigella).

label: Sweet / Vanillic
reason: Vanilla and cooked sugar are recognisably different sources of sweetness.

choices.label: Vanilla-like
choices.reference_note: Vanillin illustrates sweet vanilla and creamy associations; custard and the whole vanilla pod have additional facets. Syensqo documents the material as Rhovanil.

choices.label: Caramelised
choices.reference_note: Furaneol NAT (dsm-firmenich 943910) illustrates caramel-like sweetness with a fruity aspect; it is not a complete caramel accord.

label: Roasted / Nutty
reason: Roasted grain and dark coffee distinguish different roast impressions.

choices.label: Toasted / Nutty
choices.reference_note: Symrise Filbertone illustrates the hazelnut facet. Its roasted-hazelnut association is described in the manufacturer’s flavor discussion; it does not reproduce toast, popcorn and nuts together.

choices.label: Coffee-like
choices.reference_note: dsm-firmenich Coffee Espresso SFE 918743 is an identifiable coffee extract with roast and burnt-wood facets. Other coffee extracts can differ.

label: Boozy
reason: Separate fruity spirit sweetness from an oak-cask impression.

choices.label: Rum-like
choices.reference_note: dsm-firmenich Rum SFE 978907 is a named extract described as brown rum. It illustrates the rum direction, not every spirit or molasses nuance.

choices.label: Cask-like
choices.reference_note: IFF Oakwood CO₂ MD 40% in TEC illustrates oak-barrel wood with smoky, vanilla and rum facets. It is not a complete whisky accord.

label: Tonka / Almond
reason: The paired source label contains two distinct recognition directions.

choices.label: Sweet hay / Tonka
choices.reference_note: IFF Tonka Bean Absolute illustrates hay-like sweetness with almond and vanilla facets; it is a natural extract, not an unspecified tonka blend.

choices.label: Almond-like
choices.reference_note: Benzaldehyde illustrates the bitter-almond/cherry-kernel facet. Marzipan is a familiar comparison, not a complete match to the molecule.

label: Incense
reason: Fresh resin and burnt incense are useful contrasting impressions.

choices.label: Fresh frankincense
choices.reference_note: IFF Olibanum Oil is distilled frankincense resin. Its citrus and resin facets support the fresh direction; it is not burnt incense smoke.

choices.label: Incense smoke
choices.reference_note: Guaiacol illustrates the smoky facet only. IFF documents its use for smoke; this molecule does not reproduce the resin, ash and smoke of a whole incense accord.

label: Dark Balsamic
reason: A compact myrrh comparison is useful without manufacturing distinctions.

choices.label: Myrrh-like
choices.reference_note: IFF Myrrh Resinoid MD illustrates sweet resin and liquorice facets. The specified molecularly distilled extract differs from myrrh essential oil.

label: Warm Resin
reason: Keep a clear benzoin comparison; vanilla already has its own gourmand branch.

choices.label: Benzoin-like
choices.reference_note: IFF Benzoin Siam resinoid illustrates sweet vanilla-like balsam with resinous and cinnamic facets.

label: Amber
reason: Contrast vanilla-led and labdanum-led versions of the traditional sweet resin accord.

choices.label: Soft sweet amber
choices.reference_note: Benzoin Siam illustrates the sweet resin facet of soft amber. It is one material, not a complete vanilla–benzoin–labdanum amber blend.

choices.label: Resinous / Leathery
choices.reference_note: IFF Labdanum Resinoid illustrates resinous amber with leather-like facets. It does not represent every amber perfume.

label: Sweet / Cured
reason: Keep one clear cured-leaf recognition direction; dry leaf remains in its own realm.

choices.label: Sweet cured leaf
choices.reference_note: Biolandes Tabac Deco P83913100000 is an absolute from air-cured burley leaves. It illustrates cured tobacco; molasses, dried fruit and flavored pipe tobacco remain broader comparisons.

label: Fresh Rose
reason: A recognisable petal comparison is enough within this already narrow character.

choices.label: Rose petals
choices.reference_note: Phenylethyl alcohol illustrates a rose-like floral facet; it does not reproduce all the green, spicy and fruity nuances of a rose.

label: Citrus Floral
reason: Flower and leafy cologne directions are useful distinct comparisons.

choices.label: Orange flower
choices.reference_note: Givaudan Neroli Oil Tunisia is distilled bitter-orange blossom, illustrating the fresh floral direction. Orange-flower absolute is a separate extraction.

choices.label: Leafy cologne
choices.reference_note: IFF Petitgrain Bigarade Oil Tunisia is distilled from leaves and twigs; its green citrus-floral character illustrates the leafy direction.

label: Airy Floral
reason: Preserve the edited Airy Floral parent: one transparent jasmine continuation is coherent.

choices.label: Light jasmine
choices.reference_note: Hedione illustrates a transparent jasmine-like floral facet with citrus freshness. This is an airy association, not a claim about perfume strength or duration.

label: White / Heady
reason: Different rich white flowers help refine an otherwise very broad character.

choices.label: Jasmine-like
choices.reference_note: IFF Jasmin Absolute Egypt, from Jasminum grandiflorum, illustrates rich jasmine with fruity and indolic facets; other jasmine extracts differ.

choices.label: Orange-blossom-like
choices.reference_note: IFF Orange Flower Absolute Tunisia illustrates warm blossom with honeyed and fruity facets. The optional grape comparison is not a claim that the entire extract smells of grape.

label: Spicy Floral
reason: Clove-like petals and creamy ylang are distinct useful floral-spice comparisons.

choices.label: Carnation-like
choices.reference_note: IFF Carnation Absolute Egypt is a named extract with a clove-like floral facet; it also has green and herbaceous aspects.
choices.print_text: Carnation: petals with a clove hint

choices.label: Ylang-like
choices.reference_note: IFF Ylang Ylang Oil Complete Madagascar illustrates spicy fruit and warm floral facets with a creamy background; other distillation grades differ.

label: Iris / Powdery
reason: Rooty makeup powder and sweet violet offer different powdery floral comparisons.

choices.label: Orris-like
choices.reference_note: IFF Orris Absolute Italy is obtained from iris rhizomes and illustrates powdery floral and woody facets. It is not iris-petal scent.

choices.label: Violet-like
choices.reference_note: BASF Methylionone 70 illustrates a violet/orris floral facet with soft woody and fruity aspects. Violet sweets remain a familiar comparison, not a full candy accord.

label: Orchard Fruit
reason: Crisp apple/pear and fleshy stone fruit are useful familiar distinctions.

choices.label: Apple / Pear
choices.reference_note: IFF Fructone illustrates the apple-like facet. It also has tropical-fruit aspects; it is not a full apple–pear blend or a natural fruit oil.

choices.label: Peach / Apricot
choices.reference_note: Givaudan Nectaryl illustrates nectarine, peach and apricot with a lactonic facet. It is a named molecule, not a natural fruit extract.

label: Tropical
reason: Pineapple and mango offer readily understood contrasting tropical impressions.

choices.label: Pineapple-like
choices.reference_note: Symrise Allyl Caproate (allyl hexanoate) illustrates pineapple-like fruitiness; it does not contain every fresh-pineapple facet.

choices.label: Mango-like
choices.reference_note: IFF Tropicalia is a named molecule used for tropical-fruit effects including mango. It illustrates one fruity facet, not a complete ripe-mango reconstruction.

label: Jammy / Berry
reason: Freshly cooked berries and dark dried fruit are different useful refinements.

choices.label: Berry jam
choices.reference_note: dsm-firmenich documents Furaneol NAT 943910 for jam-like fruit effects. It illustrates cooked-fruit sweetness rather than a complete raspberry-jam accord.

choices.label: Plum / Dried fruit
choices.reference_note: IFF Davana Oil illustrates sweet dried-fruit character, with apricot and hay facets. Plum, raisin and prune are broader recognition comparisons.

label: Sulphurous
reason: Keep a recognisable blackcurrant-bud route rather than adding pungency for its own sake.

choices.label: Blackcurrant bud
choices.reference_note: Biolandes Blackcurrant Absolute F0424 comes from buds. Its French product description explicitly documents powerful green sulphurous facets; catty is an optional smell comparison, not ammonia.

label: Lactonic
reason: Coconut milk and creamy peach show that lactonic is not only coconut.

choices.label: Coconut milk
choices.reference_note: Givaudan Methyl Laitone 10% in DPG illustrates creamy coconut milk. It is a named lactone preparation, not an aldehyde.

choices.label: Creamy peach
choices.reference_note: A specified Givaudan reference combination: 50 parts Nectaryl plus 50 parts Methyl Laitone 10% in DPG. The manufacturer presents this pairing as peach-cheesecake-like; it illustrates creamy fruit, not all dairy or peach scents.
